keyIdea:
**Addition formulae:**
$$\sin(A \pm B) \equiv \sin A\cos B \pm \cos A\sin B$$
$$\cos(A \pm B) \equiv \cos A\cos B \mp \sin A\sin B$$
$$\tan(A \pm B) \equiv \frac{\tan A \pm \tan B}{1 \mp \tan A\tan B}$$
(note the sign swap in cos and in the tan denominator).

**Double angle formulae** (put $B = A$):
$$\sin 2A \equiv 2\sin A\cos A, \qquad \tan 2A \equiv \frac{2\tan A}{1 - \tan^2 A}$$
$$\cos 2A \equiv \cos^2 A - \sin^2 A \equiv 2\cos^2 A - 1 \equiv 1 - 2\sin^2 A$$

**Exact values:** write e.g. $75° = 45° + 30°$ or $15° = 45° - 30°$.

**Equations and identities:** choose the version of $\cos 2A$ that matches the other terms (e.g. $1 - 2\sin^2 A$ if the equation has $\sin A$), giving a quadratic in one function. Use the quadrant of $A$ to fix signs when finding $\cos A$ from $\sin A$.

**Further identities** (US Precalculus), all derived from the formulae above: half-angle $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\theta}{2}}$, $\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\theta}{2}}$ (sign from the quadrant of $\frac{\theta}{2}$); power-reducing $\sin^2\theta \equiv \frac{1}{2}(1 - \cos 2\theta)$, $\cos^2\theta \equiv \frac{1}{2}(1 + \cos 2\theta)$; product-to-sum, e.g. $\sin A\cos B \equiv \frac{1}{2}\left[\sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\right]$; and sum-to-product, e.g. $\sin P + \sin Q \equiv 2\sin\frac{P + Q}{2}\cos\frac{P - Q}{2}$.
